introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Draw a simple labelled diagram of the human ear. *[4 marks]*

(ii) Name one factor that causes hearing to deteriorate. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Diagram (to be drawn by the candidate).** A simple labelled diagram shows three parts:

- **Outer ear:** the **pinna** (ear flap) collecting sound and the **auditory canal (ear canal)**, ending at the **eardrum (tympanic membrane)**.
- **Middle ear:** an air-filled cavity containing the three small bones, the **ossicles** (the **hammer (malleus)**, the **anvil (incus)** and the **stirrup (stapes)**), which transmit and amplify the vibrations of the eardrum to the **oval window**; the **Eustachian tube** joins the middle ear to the throat and equalises the pressure.
- **Inner ear:** the fluid-filled, snail-shaped **cochlea**, which contains the sensory hair cells and turns the vibrations into nerve impulses; the **semicircular canals** (balance); the **auditory nerve** carrying the impulses to the brain.

**(ii) A factor that causes hearing to deteriorate.** **Prolonged exposure to loud noise** (loud music, machines): the intense vibrations damage the sensory hair cells of the cochlea, which do not regenerate. (Other acceptable answers: ageing; ear infections; a build-up of ear wax; a damaged eardrum; certain drugs.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) MRI is one form of non-invasive diagnostic imaging.

(i) Write in full MRI. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Write down two advantages and two disadvantages of MRI. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** MRI stands for **Magnetic Resonance Imaging**.

**(ii) Advantages (any two):**

1. It uses **no ionising radiation** (radio waves and magnetic fields only), so it is safe for repeated use and for children.
2. It gives **excellent contrast between different soft tissues** (brain, muscle, organs), with detailed images.
3. Images can be produced in **any plane** and in three dimensions.

**Disadvantages (any two):**

1. The equipment is **very expensive** to buy and to run.
2. The very **strong magnetic field** makes it **unsuitable for patients with metal implants, pacemakers** or metal fragments in the body, and metal objects must be kept out of the room.
3. A scan is **slow** (it can take many minutes), the patient must stay still in a narrow tube, which can cause **claustrophobia**, and the machine is **noisy**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) During ultrasonic probe a gel is often applied on the spot where it is performed? Explain why this is done.

(ii) Explain why ultrasound is not likely to replace x-rays completely in medical diagnoses. *[4 marks for (c)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Why the gel is used.** Air and body tissue have very **different acoustic impedances**. If there is a layer of air between the probe and the skin, almost all the ultrasound would be **reflected** at the air-skin boundary and very little would enter the body. The **gel fills the gaps** (it removes the air) and has an acoustic impedance close to that of the skin, so the ultrasound is **transmitted into the body** (and the echoes come back into the probe) with little loss at the surface.

**(ii) Why ultrasound will not replace x-rays completely.**

- **Bones and air-filled organs** (the lungs) reflect or absorb almost all the ultrasound, so ultrasound **cannot image bones, the lungs or structures behind them**, while x-rays are strongly absorbed by bone and pass through soft tissue, giving clear images of **fractures** and of the **chest**.
- The **resolution** of ultrasound images (limited by the wavelength) is **lower** than that of x-ray images for the fine detail of dense structures, and x-rays can image the whole body quickly.

Therefore the two techniques **complement** each other: each is better suited to certain parts of the body and certain diagnoses.
